barriers.description: Designers lacked control over the implementation of the third-party FatSecret app, constraining how the companion app could integrate and navigate across apps.
barriers.justification: This external dependency limited the designers' ability to manage cross-app navigation and to produce seamless design solutions and integrations required for effortless logging (process-level: manage user understanding; operational-level: produce design solutions, understand context of use).
barriers.reference_excerpt: While we lack control over the implementation of the FatSecret app, users can navigate backward using the built-in back navigation feature on both iOS and Android devices.

barriers.description: The FatSecret API did not provide timestamps for self-monitored data, forcing the research team to append timestamps in their backend to obtain the instrumentation needed for the adaptive intervention.
barriers.justification: This API limitation created additional engineering work and constrained designers' ability to straightforwardly gather temporally precise data necessary for specifying user requirements and for supporting the adaptive trigger algorithm (operational-level: specify user requirements; process-level: integrate feedback & iteration).
barriers.reference_excerpt: In addition, the FatSecret API does not include timestamps for self-monitored weight, caloric intake, or physical activity. However, the inclusion of timestamps is crucial for supporting the implementation and evaluation of our adaptive weight maintenance intervention... Thus, in our backend system, we appended timestamps to the data collected in FatSecret and BodyTrace when requesting data from those applications’ servers.

barriers.description: Delays in data synchronization between MyTrack+ and FatSecret disrupted expected real-time integration during pilot testing.
barriers.justification: Synchronization delays impeded evaluation and understanding of real-world use (operational-level: evaluate designs; process-level: manage user understanding and facilitate user involvement), requiring backend changes and limiting accurate assessment of the dual-app experience.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Notably, nearly all participants expressed concerns regarding the delay in data synchronization between MyTrack+ and FatSecret. To address this issue, we modified our Cloud Functions to request data from FatSecret’s server whenever the companion app is refreshed, effectively achieving G1.

barriers.description: The team used convenience sampling of university students for early usability testing instead of target users, which risked producing non-representative feedback and a local optimum design.
barriers.justification: Recruiting non-target participants limited designers' ability to manage evolving, accurate user understanding and to validate designs under realistic conditions (process-level: manage user understanding; operational-level: evaluate designs), potentially biasing iterative changes.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Although Computer Science students were not our main target users, according to Nielsen (49), involving students in the domain of interest from a local university in usability testing can still yield valuable feedback. We chose to recruit students as convenience samples (50) because (1) they are easier to reach and more readily available and (2) they could also be potential users of weight management apps.

barriers.description: The team did not perform a comprehensive analysis of semi-structured interviews and usability questionnaire responses, limiting the depth of evaluation and learning from pilot data.
barriers.justification: This omission constrained the designers' ability to integrate feedback, perform rigorous evaluation, and derive generalizable design requirements (process-level: integrate feedback & iteration; operational-level: evaluate designs; specify user requirements).
barriers.reference_excerpt: Second, it is important to note that we did not perform a comprehensive analysis of the conversations in our semi-structured interviews and measures of usability from questionnaire responses.

barriers.description: Project priorities required trade-offs favoring trial instrumentation and speed over richer commercial-level features, constraining the scope of design improvements responsive to some user preferences.
barriers.justification: Prioritizing the clinical trial's progress limited the team's ability to address broader user expectations and add more comprehensive functionality, reducing their capacity to address holistic experience and to produce broader design solutions (process-level: address holistic experience; operational-level: produce design solutions).
barriers.reference_excerpt: Not meeting these expectations may impact the app's usability, but trade-offs were necessary to achieve our main design goal: effectively supporting the implementation of our team’s specific adaptive weight intervention and prioritizing the progress of our clinical trial aimed at evaluating the intervention’s effectiveness.
